blocks.text: Release overview

iOS 11.0 was publicly released on September 19, 2017. The annual platform release redesigned core system experiences while giving iPad a substantially broader set of multitasking and file-management tools.

The public feature set included a rebuilt App Store, the Files app and expanded iPad multitasking, ARKit, new Camera and Photos capabilities, Do Not Disturb While Driving, richer Maps guidance, and a redesigned Control Center.
Release overview
iOS 11.0.1 reached the public channel on September 26, 2017. Apple characterized it only as a bug-fix and improvement update for iPhone and iPad.

Apple’s surviving consumer note does not enumerate the individual fixes. Its security advisory says the release carried the security content of iOS 11, so this record makes no claim about new CVE-specific changes.
Release overview
iOS 11.0.2 was publicly released on October 3, 2017. This maintenance release focused on a short list of call-audio, photo-library, and encrypted-mail attachment problems.
Apple documented fixes for crackling during calls on a small number of iPhone 8 models, photos that could become hidden, and S/MIME-encrypted mail attachments that failed to open.
Release overview
iOS 11.0.3 reached the public channel on October 11, 2017. Its documented scope centered on two hardware-interaction problems affecting specific iPhone models and display configurations.
The release restored audio and haptic feedback on some iPhone 7 models and addressed unresponsive touch input on some iPhone 6s devices fitted with non-genuine replacement displays.
Release overview
iOS 11.1 was publicly released on October 31, 2017. It combined a visible emoji expansion with accessibility, Photos, app-switching, and security corrections.

The update added more than 70 emoji, restored the 3D Touch edge gesture for the app switcher, improved several VoiceOver and braille workflows, repaired Photos behaviors, and delivered new CVE-tracked security fixes.
Release overview
iOS 11.1.1 reached the public channel on November 9, 2017. Apple’s consumer notes identify two focused corrections involving keyboard autocorrection and voice activation for Siri.
The maintenance update fixed an autocorrect problem and a condition in which the “Hey Siri” trigger could stop working. Apple’s advisory says it retained the security content of iOS 11.1.
Release overview
iOS 11.1.2 was publicly released on November 16, 2017. It targeted two iPhone X display and camera behaviors while retaining the iOS 11.1 security baseline.
Apple documented a fix for temporary touch unresponsiveness after a rapid temperature drop and a correction for distortion in iPhone X Live Photos and videos.
Release overview

iOS 11.2 was publicly released on December 2, 2017. It prepared support for Apple Pay Cash, enabled faster wireless charging on supported iPhones, and bundled interface, reliability, accessibility, and security work.

blocks.text: Release overview
iOS 11.2.1 reached the public channel on December 13, 2017. The narrowly scoped update repaired shared-user remote access in Home and included a documented HomeKit security correction.

Apple’s consumer note says the release fixed a bug that could disable remote access for shared Home users. The corresponding advisory records improved validation for a HomeKit message-handling issue tracked as CVE-2017-13903.
Release overview

iOS 11.3 was publicly released on March 29, 2018. The update paired new battery-health controls with ARKit 1.5, privacy disclosures, Health Records, Business Chat, new Animoji, and a large security set.

blocks.text: Battery Health exposed capacity and performance-management information on supported iPhones. ARKit gained vertical-plane and image detection, while regional and device limits applied to Health Records, Business Chat, Animoji, and several other additions.

blocks.text: Release overview
iOS 11.4 was publicly released on May 29, 2018. Its headline additions were AirPlay 2 multi-room audio, HomePod stereo-pair setup, Messages in iCloud, and a broad set of security fixes.

AirPlay 2 coordinated playback and controls across compatible speakers, HomePod gained stereo-pair support, and Messages in iCloud synchronized stored conversations and deletions across signed-in devices with end-to-end encryption.
Release overview
iOS 11.4.1 reached the public channel on July 9, 2018. It combined two user-facing reliability fixes with a documented security update across networking, system, and web components.

The release restored some users’ ability to see the last known AirPods location in Find My iPhone, improved Exchange synchronization for mail, contacts, and notes, and addressed multiple CVE-tracked vulnerabilities.
